desc: The matrix contains only 0s and 1s. Find the largest square block of cells that consists entirely of 1s, and return its area (side length squared). If the matrix has no 1 at all, return 0.
hints: Checking every square at every position works but is slow for large grids. Try to reuse information from neighbouring cells.
Let side[r][c] be the side of the largest all-ones square whose bottom-right corner is cell (r, c).
If the cell is 0 the value is 0; otherwise it is 1 + min(side[r-1][c], side[r][c-1], side[r-1][c-1]). The answer is the square of the largest value.
editorial: Fix the bottom-right corner (r, c) of a square. It can have side k only if the cell is 1 and the three squares of side k-1 that end just above, just to the left and diagonally up-left of it are all-ones as well. That yields side[r][c] = 1 + min(side[r-1][c], side[r][c-1], side[r-1][c-1]) for a 1-cell, and 0 for a 0-cell.

Out-of-range neighbours count as 0, so the first row and column are just copies of the matrix. Track the maximum side seen while filling the table, and return its square. Keeping only the previous row and the old diagonal value reduces memory to O(n); time is O(m · n).
